          Chelsea vs Arsenal Prediction: WSL Preview
        
      
                          
                      Sep 25, 2026
          
                      Chloe Horswill / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
While they are both unbeaten, Chelsea and Arsenal have not been at their best in 2026-27. Can either side apply pressure on Manchester City? We preview a heavyweight showdown at Stamford Bridge that could have major ramifications for the early WSL title race.
Heading into Matchday 4, only one team in the Women's Super League have a perfect record, with champions Manchester City setting the pace in 2026-27.

Chelsea were the pre-season favourites for the title, winning 40.8% of the Opta supercomputer's simulations, with Arsenal also expected to be challengers. But neither have matched their rivals' fast start.
There is still a very long way to go in the title race and both teams are unbeaten, but Sunday's clash at Stamford Bridge already feels pivotal for Chelsea and Arsenal.

Chelsea come into this match after a narrow 1-0 win over Austria Wien in the Women's Champions League on Wednesday, while Arsenal prevailed by the same scoreline against Køge on Tuesday, needing a 93rd-minute Mariona Caldentey penalty to secure the three points.
So, can either of them kick into gear in the WSL this weekend?
After a disappointing 1-1 draw with Aston Villa, Chelsea have strung together two wins, hammering Manchester United 5-0 before beating Birmingham City 2-0.
While they looked comfortable against Eva Olid's struggling United, there was plenty to be desired against Birmingham, namely their finishing.
They accumulated 3.9 expected goals (xG) from 22 shots, with eight of those on target and one hitting the woodwork. They also recorded five Opta-defined ‘big chances' but could only score twice.
Melvine Malard came off the bench to net on her WSL debut for the club in the second half, settling the nerves after they failed to get the goals their early dominance deserved.
But while there may be question marks over their chance conversion, they have started the season well defensively, conceding just one goal and keeping two clean sheets.
No team have faced fewer shots (14), while the Blues have also limited their opponents to just 1.3 expected goals against (xGA).

With a record like that, if they score the first goal, Arsenal could be in trouble; Chelsea are unbeaten in their last 45 WSL matches when leading at any stage (W38 D7), the longest run in the competition's history.
Arsenal, meanwhile, were expected to pick up where they left off at the end of last season, but it has been a stuttering start to their title charge.
They edged a 1-0 win over Brighton on the opening weekend, before drawing with Crystal Palace and Man Utd.

At this point, they are hoping to avoid matching an unwanted record: the Gunners could win as few as five points from their first four matches for the second time in the last three seasons after 2024-25, when the fourth game was a defeat to Chelsea (W1 D2).
In the WSL, they have netted just two goals – only promoted duo Palace and Charlton Athletic have scored fewer (both one) – and have massively underperformed their 5.9 xG.
The Gunners' shot conversion rate of 3.3% this term is also the worst seen in the WSL since bottom-of-the-league Yeovil Town in 2017-18 (2.2%).
They rank fourth for shots (60), with 10 of those classed as ‘big' chances, and have had 22 attempts on target.
It was a familiar story against Koge as they racked up 19 attempts worth 1.9 xG – a figure inflated by their late penalty – but only two of those shots were on target.
